name: Sugar Commons
award: 2025 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Völker's Sugar Commons is a planned three-story, 54-unit family apartment building for households earning 30% to 70% AMI at 777 N. 4th Street in Sterling. It won 2025 Round Two federal 4% and state housing tax credits from CHFA and is billed as the first tax credit family housing in Sterling in over 25 years.
why_it_matters: It is a rare rural Eastern Plains 4% bond deal. It has state support (tax credits plus a $2.3M Prop 123 loan selected in July 2026), but local approval is unresolved: Sterling City Council's 3-2 vote on its conditional use was recorded as failing in October 2025.

status.label: Credits awarded; local land-use approval and closing not confirmed
status.detail: A motion to approve the conditional use failed on 2025-10-14: the vote was 3-2 with two members absent. The hearing returned to the council agendas of 2025-11-18 and 2025-11-25, but minutes for those meetings are not posted online, so the outcome is not public. OEDIT preliminarily selected the project for a $2,299,500 Prop 123 loan on 2026-07-21. No closing, building permit or groundbreaking record was found. The applicant had targeted a financial closing by October 2026.

next_step: Watch for Sterling City Council minutes from November 2025 showing the conditional use outcome, a rezoning to R3, and a financial closing or building permit in late 2026.

key_numbers.meaning: 18 one-bedroom, 21 two-bedroom and 15 three-bedroom units at 30% to 70% AMI; 16 of them at or below 50% AMI.
About $10.6M over 10 years, plus $1,324,619 of accelerated state credit and $10,250,000 of CHFA bonds.
LIHTC gap loan from the Affordable Housing Financing Fund, preliminarily approved 2026-07-21; final terms set in underwriting.
The Planning Commission had recommended approval. The outcome of the November 2025 rehearing is not in posted records.

facts.value: One three-story, wood-frame walk-up building on a slab, with shingle roof and cementitious siding. Average unit sizes 535 (1BR), 750 (2BR) and 936 (3BR) sq ft. Three-bedroom units have in-unit washers and dryers; the others share a laundry room

Infill site in a qualified census tract, formerly a one-story brick building and parking lots that have been demolished. The applicant gives 3.97 acres; the architect gives 2.10 acres and 25.7 units per acre
Community Business (CB). The council motion paired the conditional use with a map amendment to High Density Residential (R3) before construction, after the developer acquires the site
Executed purchase and sale agreement, per the applicant
South-facing family courtyard with play areas, community room, fitness room, pet amenities, on-site management, controlled access, EV charging
NGBS Silver target, at least six EV-ready spaces, electrification-ready and solar-ready design, planned solar garden participation
Prairie Express local bus runs next to the site (every 30 minutes); CDOT Bustang regional service links Sterling to Denver and Greeley
Service coordination by the property management team, funded in the operating budget, with referrals to nearby agencies such as the Family Resource Center and Centennial Mental Health Center
About $16M, per the architect's project sheet
Planned exemption through a partnership with the Sterling Housing Authority, per the applicant

background.text: The applicant says the project came out of work with City of Sterling staff, who had earlier identified the property as a good site for family affordable housing.

The Planning Commission recommended approval of the conditional use on 2025-09-03. At the 2025-10-14 council hearing one member of the public spoke against it. The motion to approve the conditional use, with a rezoning from CB to R3 before construction, got three yes and two no votes and was recorded as failing.

Two of seven council members were absent on 2025-10-14, and a three-yes, two-abstain consent agenda vote also failed that night. This suggests four votes are needed to pass (inferred; the minutes do not state the rule).
The conditional use hearing was placed on the 2025-11-18 agenda as new business and on the 2025-11-25 agenda as unfinished business.
The applicant had expected the conditional use and a parking reduction to be approved before the end of October 2025, with building permits issued in time for a financial closing by October 2026.
The market study found a 96% occupancy rate, an 11.7% overall capture rate and lease-up of about 15 units a month. It noted the 60% and 70% AMI rents are slightly above comparable properties.

The primary market area has three LIHTC projects with 173 income-restricted units, including the senior-only Deer Run Apartments next to the site. The nearest LIHTC property outside it is more than 35 miles away in Brush.
The budget includes housing for the construction superintendent and project engineer because of the rural location.
The Phase I environmental assessment found no recognized environmental conditions.

discrepancies.text: The application sought $11,500,000 of bonds, while CHFA's award report lists $10,250,000.
The application describes a 3.97-acre site, while the architect lists 91,575 square feet (2.10 acres).
The application says proper zoning is in place, while the council motion required a rezoning from Community Business to High Density Residential (R3) before construction.
